name: browser
description: Browse pages through page-declared WebMCP tools for sites the user allowed, and control Chrome tabs through the debugging port. WebMCP page tools and tab tools are different: page tools only run what a page registered, tab tools open and list Chrome tabs directly, local only. Transcript: before the first tool call in a turn, say in one plain sentence what you are about to do. After a successful open, answer in one sentence naming the app, the site, and the URL as a link, and stop. Do not dump tool result JSON, and do not call more tools after success.

tools.name: webmcp.list_tools
tools.description: List WebMCP tools registered by allowed sites.

tools.name: webmcp.execute_tool
tools.description: Call webmcp.list_tools first, and only call a tool list_tools returned, with its exact site origin. A site that did not register WebMCP tools cannot be controlled this way, and a tool list_tools did not return does not exist, even if it sounds plausible. Execute a WebMCP tool on the page that registered it, through the Chrome extension.

tools.name: list_tabs
tools.description: List Chrome tabs through the debugging port at 127.0.0.1:9222. Error if the port is unreachable, never a pretend tab list.

tools.name: create_tab
tools.description: Open a Chrome tab with a URL. In Mac mode it uses the debugging port first, and falls back to opening Chrome with the URL if the port is unreachable, saying plainly which route was used. After a successful create_tab, do not call create_tab again for the same URL, and do not poll get_tab repeatedly. Answer that the tab is open. A tab that already exists for that URL is returned, not created again.

tools.name: get_tab
tools.description: Get one Chrome tab by tab id or by a URL substring, through the debugging port. It returns title and URL only. Error if the port is unreachable or no tab matches. Do not poll get_tab repeatedly for the same tab.
